text:
ari: noticed something odd in the latency dashboard for /v1/generate — p95 jumped ~60ms last night but p99 barely moved, p50 shifted downwards. anyone else seeing this?

samira: saw that too, started after we flipped the routing policy to prefer cached variants. looks more pronounced in eu-west.

ivan: can you paste the panel query or screenshot? are we accidentally aggregating across model variants?

ari: panel query is: 
```sql
select endpoint, quantile(latency,0.5) as p50, quantile(latency,0.95) as p95, quantile(latency,0.99) as p99
from request_metrics
where route = '/v1/generate'
group by endpoint
```

mia: quick hypothesis — KV-cache fastpath returns much lower per-token latency but we rewrote the route tag on a hit. that means the dashboard might be mixing samples from original route + cached variant inconsistently.

samira: yep. routing change added a cached_variant fallback that rewrites route_name only on miss, so hits keep a different tag. sample origins are now inconsistent.

ivan: that would explain a lower p50 (lots of fast cache hits) while p95 rises if some clients still hit main path and those tails dominate the high-percentiles. cross-variant blending can produce weird non-monotonic shapes.

ari: short-term: can we add cache_hit as a dimension on the dashboard so we can split the series?

mia: we have cache_hit boolean in the metrics. quick fix: change the panel to `group by cache_hit, endpoint` and render two lines. longer term we should preserve original route_tag for cache hits so dashboards keep semantics.

samira: I'll open an ops ticket to preserve route_tag on fastpath and run a small canary. meanwhile I'll annotate the dashboard legend: "includes cached variants (broken out by cache_hit)". @deploy-bot can you schedule synthetic-run on eu-west to reproduce?

deploy-bot: scheduled synthetic run: `synthetic /v1/generate` on eu-west at 3723457000. will post results here when done. :robot_face:  

ivan: also suggest using tdigest rollups keyed by endpoint+variant (or cache_hit) so quantiles don't merge across incompatible sample origins. low-sample merges are noisy.

ari: totally. adding two checklist items to the rollout playbook: 1) preserve route_tag on fastpath; 2) add cache_hit dimension to latency dashboards.

samira: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/telemetry/merge/582 — includes test plan and dashboard update.

ari: LGTM, merge after canary green. :thumbsup:
